# texarkanine

> Author: Texarkanine

## Posts

- [Just Try the Thing](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/08/01/just-try-the-thing.md): Agents collapsed the cost of trying a new tool and multiplied the upside of even small gains. Bezos' two-way doors still apply - but the old bias against trying is now the expensive choice.
- [You're Absolutely Right](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/06/30/absolutely-right.md): The 'You're absolutely right!' meme is about sycophancy, but the deeper itch is accountability - models can course-correct instantly and without suffering, but humans keep reaching for punishment anyway.
- [It's Not a "Nitpick" if You're Wrong](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/06/06/not-a-nitpick.md): The complaint that AI reviewers are nitpicky smuggles in a false premise. I went and checked the findings. They were real, the code was bad, and it was probably always bad, so why isn't that signal acted on?
- [The Magnificent 7 BSODs and the Hateful 8th to 11th](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/05/11/magnificent-7-bsods.md): Eleven different stop codes over seventy-four days were eleven angles on a single dying CPU. A Patch Tuesday update only took the blame - but wasn't the cause.
- [The Suite Life of Bobs and Code](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/05/10/slobac.md): SLOBAC delivers principles for good tests, a taxonomy of test smells, safe refactoring workflows, and an agent skill to audit and clean up sprawling AI-generated test suites.
- [The Elgato Streamdeck for Shell Aliases on Headless Linux](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/04/19/elgato-alias.md): Adding an Elgato Streamdeck to my headless Linux server to manifest shell aliases and system status in the physical world... all because I have too much stuff plugged in for my circuit breaker to handle.
- [Sub-Agents aren't Agents - They're Skills but Worse](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/03/30/subagents-arent-agents.md): Sub-Agents are syntactic sugar over skills with one baked-in assumption about execution context that should be the caller's decision.
- [The Load-Bearing Pipeline Was Human](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/03/21/the-load-bearing-pipeline-was-human.md): A specification-to-code pipeline that worked for decades doesn't stop working because you swapped the executors; it stops working when you rip out the stages.
- [The Adeptus Mechanicus Bootcamp: A Gentle Seduction](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/03/14/adeptus-mechanicus-bootcamp-gentle-seduction.md)
- [Context to Ashes, Skills to Dust](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/03/09/context-to-ashes-skills-to-dust.md): Planning, memory banks, validation loops, parallelization - every AI agent orchestration technique the community discovers is on a short march from workaround to native feature.
- [Pink Margarine](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/03/01/pink-margarine.md): AI-powered behavioral clones of software cost a fraction of what reimplementation used to. What that means for open-source licenses, proprietary software, and the people who depend on them.
- [It's Model Context Protocol, Not Agent Context Protocol](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/02/23/model-context-protocol-not-agent-context-protocol.md): A framework for evaluating when MCP tools earn their context-window tokens and when the model's existing shell access & intuition makes them expensive dead weight.
- [.gitignore is not .agentignore](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/02/22/gitignore-is-not-agentignore.md): Your agent needs to see content like generated output, node_modules, and personal config that git rightfully ignores. The current crop of tool-specific ignore files needs a real standard.
- [Stop Doing AGENTS.md](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/02/12/stop-doing-agents-md.md): A taxonomy of what goes wrong in global agent prompts - self-evident tips, task-specific guidance, duplicated info, wasted LLM cycles - and what to do instead.
- [Good Money Should Be Worthless](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/02/11/good-money-should-be-worthless.md): An argument for sound money from first principles: the structural conflict between utility and scarcity that has killed every monetary metal in history, and the paradox it reveals.
- [The Load-Bearing Rate Limiter Was Human](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/02/06/the-load-bearing-rate-limiter-was-human.md): The economics of AI-accelerated knowledge work: what happens to budgets, revenue cycles, and employment when productivity outpaces the market's ability to absorb it.
- [I Finally Coded So Hard I Ralphed](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/01/25/i-finally-coded-so-hard-i-ralphed.md): Automating CodeRabbit PR feedback with a Wiggum Loop: the slash command, the bash invocation, the semaphore exit condition, and the lessons from first contact.
- [The Use Case for AI Coding Agent Slash Commands](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/01/23/use-case-for-ai-coding-agent-slash-commands.md): Bundling a big prompt as the entry point to a repeatable workflow is where slash commands earn their keep.
- [All It Took Was Broken Firmware](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/01/17/all-it-took-was-broken-firmware.md): A petcare hub that can't survive a network switch, DD-WRT VLAN isolation, iptables one-way firewall rules, and PiHole DNS with NAT exemption for building an isolated IoT subnet.
- [Tools Suck When They're Products](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2025/12/22/tools-suck-when-theyre-products.md): Tools are not products and building them *like* products results in bad tools. Nobody actually wants to use tools. They want the *result* of using the tool.
- [Tabs for Humans, Spaces for LLMs](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2025/12/05/tabs-for-humans-spaces-for-llms.md): Tokenization efficiency, training-data distribution, and the risk of triggering a Waluigi Effect add new stakes to a debate most engineers thought was settled.
- [Look at this Dog](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2025/11/25/look-at-this-dog.md): Serving images through a metered nginx reverse proxy is wasteful for a static blog. Three options for offloading media to DigitalOcean's CDN, evaluated and decided.
- [The Usen't Case for AI Coding Agent Slash Commands](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2025/11/24/usent-case-for-ai-coding-agent-slash-commands.md): Every slash command you'd write is better served by a Rule, Skill, or other Tool that the agent picks up passively. The few apparent exceptions don't survive scrutiny.
- [I Can't ai-rizz on Command](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2025/11/24/cant-ai-rizz-on-command.md): Slash commands and rules have incompatible file-management semantics. Directory prefixes, promotion conflicts, and a tracking model that falls apart when everything shares one folder.
- [We Therefore do not Recommend this Approach (to Upgrading OctoPrint's Python)](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2025/11/14/octoprint-python-upgrade-cascade.md): Python 3.13 needs glibc 2.34, glibc 2.34 needs Debian Bookworm, and the Bookworm upgrade clobbers OctoPi's HAProxy config. A three-step yak shave on a Raspberry Pi.
- [Building the Blog](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2025/11/11/building-the-blog.md): Jekyll, GitHub Actions, and the 'no style, please' theme: archives, author pages, tag indexes, and the philosophy behind a sub-1KB CSS static site.
